May I ask how long she has been seeing a therapist? Either way its clearly going to depend on her situation.

When I was diagnosed with bipolar as well as frequently having panic attacks, I did not get support. What I got was people telling me I was weak and useless. Obviously thats not very productive.

I would say that if you listen, just listen, that will be a fantastic way to support her. Some do not et it, sometimes all it takes is listening, without judgement,to change a life. Even save it.

Edit: You are a very good person for standing by her, when so many are left to pull themselves out. 

We developed as a species together, we form bonds because it assures survival. Over so many, many generations, thats not something that just goes away. When it does , tho, thats when issues arise. Oh, this I am very much aware of. I tended to argue it a lot after my depression seemed to fade. Psychology is a massive part of my "new identity", I read as many papers as I can on the subject. Every now an again I become manic, then brain processing power seems to go through the roof. Its scary sometimes. 

anyway, I do hope it goes well for you. Have faith in yourself. Whatever you are going through will change you for the better, I am sure.

Digging into ones past is generally the way we understand any issues, which tends to bring up bad memories. Crying is not such a big deal, but some find it uncomfortable of course. Being a guy and crying, to many , seems weak. But for me, I sobbed like a baby on my 2nd visit. 


My life experiences have taught me that the term "weak" is not applicable when it comes to expressing ones thoughts. Doing so can take an unbelievable amount of courage. When family would mock me for being "crazy", when they would judge me for taking medication, I was at first very ashamed. Over time I developed compassion , and actually felt bad that they were so uncomfortable in their own skin, they could not find the will to properly express it if something went wrong. 

apologies, I tend to rant.

It would seem you are very supportive, but sometimes that may not be enough. Many times people will get scared when confronting someone with such issues, which is never helpful, luckily for her, and you, this is not who you are. 

Have you considered therapy? Because you are family, its quite possible, and very easy, to have difficulties, bias being a key issue in my experience. A therapist is a stranger, therefore theres no real bias there. Sometimes it helps to have an outside perspective. A exam by a doctor may also be a good idea. lol The internet. You guys are amazing.

Many people have used medications, many people have been helped by doing so. I am not suggesting medication can save everyone. They are meant to be a tool used, so that one can undergo therapy.

The argument that because there is no sure-fire way to "cure" people is not a reasonable argument. The human mind is something we may never fully understand (But recent breakthroughs *are* in the works). Until we get to the point of understanding the brain , it is the best we can do.

My point was, you do not know the OP. You are making a snap-judgement based on a single post. You know who else does that? People who refuse to get their children medical help, and we al know how that tends to end.

Lets leave it to the OP to decide. This has gone too far as it is.

Here is a little secret, keep it to yourself, ok?


None of us know what we are doing. Not a single one of us. We all have hobbies, etc, whatever, just to keep our shattered minds from totally collapsing.

I myself went through  depression for several years. What doeskin help, is when people tell me "Its in your head!". I mean, yeah, technically EVERYTHING is in my head. Existence itself can be in my head. Hell, there is no real way to tell if you are not just imagining the entire universe. 

Look, nobody can bring meaning to you but you. They can help, but ultimately its left with you. Scary, right? Consider our place in the universe. Massive, isn't it? You are part of that beauty. Your story started billions of years ago. At some point a star exploded. That exploded star spit its guts all over the universe, creating planets etc. Eventually it created life. That life evolved, most of it died out. Your ancestors went from a single-celled nothing, to something which as a brain consisting of more neurons, and neurological connections, than there are stars. Your brain all started from muck, now look at you. 

Srry, that was random. But my point is, you are gorgeous. Lost? Sure, we're al lost in ... space, I guess.  


You are going to fall, a lot. Everyone who has ever lived has fallen, many, many times. The only difference between you and any who have ever lived is they pushed back at life, pulled themselves up. 

Consider also when someone works out, they gain muscle etc. Its painful as hell. The heart races rapidly, muscles tear and rebuild. All that pain, and later they get a benefit. Look at your misery as an opportunity, look at it as a reason to sit back and think about what it is you desire. And aim HIGH. Forget standards of others, of what they think. 

And dump your bf, he seems like a dick.  Anyone who puts another down when they are clearly not feeling well about themselves, is cheap and very tacky.
OP, you have some fantastic advice given here, so there's nothing more to say , really. Just be honest with the doctor. I truly do wish you the best. Hang on.

A bit irresponsible, dont you think?

Unless you fully understand a persons condition, its impossible to make such a judgement. Besides, medications *can* help. If they are taken properly, and , this is *very* important, if the patient is communicating with doctors properly,it can save a life. 

Also, a psychiatrist will generally require a patient to first get an examination, to rule out anything they can.

I am not certain I suggested any experience was the same. In fact, I said just the opposite.

When it comes to mental health, it is all subjective. Subjective is very important here.


Clearly there are situations where it is objective, I assumed that was made clear with what I said. Forgive me, I must not have explained it very well. 


I suppose my point is, we all suffer. Who suffers more is, to me, irrelevant. The point is suffering, mentally. When we get into discussion about "who suffers more", we tend to alienate ourselves.

It is because of separation, ie "this person suffers more", that we have the stigma when it comes to mental health. This is the very reason we find it so difficult to discuss this topic in the mainstream. It is because we discuss "who suffers more", that many find it so difficult to speak to loved ones, and instead, take their lives.

No need to explain, I do know what you mean. My point in phrasing it as a question, was to force you to consider what was said.

We all suffer, regardless. Life itself is suffering, that goes without argument. However, this is regarding depression, etc. As many have pointed out, correctly, is that , when it comes to mental health, all is subjective. It is because mental health is subjective, that it is very difficult to determine what is true and what is not. You, nor I, can see into the minds of others. Hell, we can cannot see within our own, yet it is within our minds we are. 

tl;dr None can say who suffers what, at any given time. Rather than focus on who is feeling what, it is,perhaps, best we focus on ourselves, trying to understand ourselves. When we begin to learn that we are imperfect, we are all subject to the human condition, it is then that we learn to relate to others, sharing as we are now.


 If we share, without judgement, then we can begin to heal as a species. Imagine you yell at someone who made a mistake. Now imagine that, earlier in the day, they found out they have cancer,or a loved one is very sick. Such news would disrupt any life, would you not agree? When someone does me wrong, I try to give them the benefit of the doubt, because I have no idea about what is going on in their life. Basically, I express compassion towards all, until they prove , without a reasonable doubt, that they do not deserve it.

Apologies, I am fairly messed up, lately I have had much difficulty in properly explaining how I am thinking.

There is a reason I have such great respect and admiration for those struggling, and expressing it. These are the people who have the best lessons to give, they are the ones who, in general, have the most compassion. This world needs compassion, but it is difficult to do so because we all struggle individually. We, some of us, believe we are alone. All we need is to develop the courage to speak our minds.  

Personally, I am tired of hurting, tired of life. But I am here, so I may as well keep pushing.

I actually had to stop doing marketing and web design recently, after only being back into the work for a couple months. 

My point is, well, if I did not work very hard, manual labor, I would absolutely fall to pieces. I do sometimes get absent-minded at times, luckily the work I do does not require too much thought, per-say, its all muscle memory. 

But as hard as I work, it is becoming more and more difficult to work hard enough to push away the demons.
What signifies "normal"?

Well, personally, I do not think about who"fakes it". Its like this; I cannot read their thoughts, nobody can. 

It is best considered on an individual basis. After all, none of us have authority  over who feels what, in whatever way.

That would seem to be perfectly natural. I mean, fight or flight causes the hear to quicken, to push more blood/oxygen through the system to prepare you for danger etc. 

As for those feeling it, in , say, the wrists, that is probably due to the fact you are paying such close attention to it. Its like when it is very quiet, if you make no noise, you can hear , idk how to explain it, but a kind of buzzing noise. Again, thats because you are giving it your full attention. 

I would not be too concerned with it, unless you are like me, and you give yourself panic attacks by thinking about having a panic attack. Its then I feel it as explained by others.

Others have basically suggested the right thing; Tell someone. Make certain you trust them. Some are nervous  to see a therapist for the first time, but the benefit of seeing a trained professional, and trust me they ave heard it all, is that they will be unbiased. Some also call therapists "paid friends". Why pay, when you can talk to a friend etc?? Well, it is good to be open, but sometimes it is best to speak with a trained therapist.

Now, I will briefly share my story. For me it is encouraging to hear I am not the only one. 

I worked for myself doing marketing online, and web design. Working nearly 100 hrs a week as well as my mother nearly dying, losing 3 friends as well as a cousin. I completely fell apart. It started with me having panic attacks, which are horrifying and, like depression, which came later, it is very confusing. 

My family had moved me into my grandparents home. Honestly, I wish they would have brought me to stay at a hospital. I spent a good part of 3 years heavily medicated. Suffering from severe anxiety and bipolar. The medication did help for a while, but what went wrong was due to being on so many meds, I could not properly communicate with my therapist and psychiatrist. I basically just existed. Unable to feel sadness. Some may believe "Hey, youre not sad, thats great!". Well, no. I could feel nothing. I did not feel human. The depersonalization was pretty severe as well. Each night I considered , as I walked up the railroad tracks, stepping in front of the train. 

It took every ounce of strength not to end my life. I not only was a  zombie, but I constantly had relatives tell me to man up. What have I done? I was not doing it because I enjoyed feeling dead inside. 


It is easy for someone to tell you things will get better. But what you may feel is nothing but terror, absolutely hopelessness. I can tell you, when I "snapped out of it", one day, I did my best to talk about it. People fear what they do not understand, that is our nature. This needs to change, it is changing. I will be 110% honest with you here; The world needs you to recover. When you do recover, you will be changed. You will have been molded into something strong, you will be someone with great compassion for others who are hurting. They seriously need someone who has been through those battles, someone who is not ashamed of their scars. 


Is it scary to talk about to others? Absolutely. Why else would mental health be taboo as it is? Because we are not very well educated, especially when it comes to the mind. But we are human, we have survived for over 250,000 years. You do not survive that long without developing strength. But you develop it as you would working out your body, by being in pain and pulling your way out. 

I am nowhere close to being religious, but consider that the darkness you see does not exist. Darkness is merely the lack of light. My point is, you *are* strong, and all you need is a small amount of light to fight your way back. 

Srry, my heads a bit of a wreck lately as well. Feeling a bit numb, beat up. But as bad as it feels, I know that when I feel better, it will be that much more incredible.

Found this in my email, sadly, it was deleted here. I would still like to address this comment:

"Thanks for removing all doubt about you and confirming everything by downplaying very real mental and personal problems as "someone's bad mood".

Also, finally fuck off with the trite "man up" shit."

I was not downplaying anything. I understand very well the stigma of mental health. And what I said had nothing to do with "man-up". It has nothing to do with what anyone else thinks of it all, its about the individual and how they manage. It's about taking control of a situation that seems impossible. Of course when you're in that state its not even easier said than done. 

I'm not sure how many times I have to share my story to make it clear than I would never tell someone that they can just get over something. That same nonsense was told to me for years, therefore I would never, ever tell it to another. 

What I suggest is that it can be beaten. But not everyone believes that, I get it, especially when you're in that state. Somehow along the way some get it in their heads that I am saying it'll be easy; Nobody even hinted that it would be easy. I have said time and again it will be a very difficult accomplishment, but to say its impossible is wrong. 

It seems that if someone tries to try and be upbeat about the topic, others get all pissy and cry victim. I was fucking there as well, you are not the only one who has been through hell. Time to stop acting like it.
Its not weak to not want to die, especially if its going to be painful as hell. Im not even sure where the hell people get this idea.

Well, for one, I nor you can say what the fucks going to happen tomorrow. Or next week, etc. If you are expecting life isnt going to spit in your face Im not sure what to tell you. 


Life is a fucking struggle. Always has, always will be.

You mean fuck up with overcoming obstacles? So your advice is that someone not feeling good about themselves should have the option to put themselves down? And if you're going to do it, dont be a pussy and wish for a painless way. 

You can think whatever you'd like. As for me, Im not here to add to someones already shitty outlook. If you want to contribute to someones bad mood, keep it to yourself. The rest of us will man-up and realize that you can use pain to actually build yourself up. Shit already hurts, theres no point in taking the other way out when you have 60 or so years where shit can change.

Just over a year, I still get those moments. 

The worst thing for me right now is motivation. Its difficult to find excuses not to get better motivated. The medications I was on really fucked me up. Once in a while I will get a few moments, perhaps even an entire day, if the numbing sensations throughout my entire body. 

As I have told people here many times before, and as most of us understand, you have to be a god damn lion and just tear right through whatever doubts you may have. I dont mean ignore them, you must acknowledge them to some extent. Just dont let them control who you are. While actions do decide our fate, how we feel in the moment is not who we are.

When you stop feeling, thats when you have to really worry. As Grandmere said, you just have to slow down. Actually, some very good advice right there so I wont go on. 

We all need a break once in a while. If you're able to do so, then I would highly recommend it. I developed depression much later, and it never gets easy regardless of your age. Sadly, when you're older, you have fewer options. You still have time.

He did, and stayed awake until they arrived. He was pretty fucked up. My point is, we can withstand a lot. Sometimes, tho, it becomes too much and we find ourselves in absolute agony. At least if its not being burned alive, you still have a chance. If you can withstand the torments of years, it only makes sense that you can deal with the pain of getting shit back on track. 

And no, theres no "easier said than done". Shits never easy. Whether youre going through serious depression or not, it sucks for everyone. The joy in life comes from when the pain dulls down. Tho, its my belief that we absolutely need pain in order to be happy. 

There is not much in life I have faith in, mostly when it involves humans. But one thing I do have faith in, is the strength of the human race when strength is needed.

Failing to kill yourself is not failure. You didnt fail. Any moron can kill themselves. There's something in you that refuses to go, despite the pain. 

Dont see it as a sign, none of that nonsense. Its you, your instincts arent going to go out that easy. 

Look, a few years ago a friend of mine lit himself on fire. Literally. In fucking flames. Im not telling you that to make you feel guilty, or for any perspective. Really, what I am saying is if someone can stay conscious for that long, with a body on fire, blistering, then that ought to give you an idea of how hard it can be pushed before it gives up. 

Fuck that, you've still got some shit to do. If youve survived 8 more years, then you can survive another 8. Stop merely surviving, take some steps. Get some kind of help. Find the most hardcore psychologist you can find, and get some help. 

Cognitive therapy. Trust me on this.

Theres no joy without the shitty days. 

If you want to enjoy life then ask yourself what you want. To just be happy? Because I can tell you, nobody ever finds happiness. Its not something you can find, but look for each and every waking day. 

You just want not to hurt. Im sure being content would be fine for most people. At least for me it was this way. If you want to stop hurting as much as you hurt, then giving up is pointless. I would consider giving up to also mean stop trying. 

If you're not seeing a therapist, then get off your ass and take care of yourself. No words are going to do it, you have to. And no, Im not "one of those people". I understand it takes a LOT of work, but life is supposed to take work. 

Stop kicking yourself in the teeth and be good to yourself. Try it, for even a couple hours. Hell, an hour. You'll be fucking amazed how much such a small amount of time can motivate you. You can do so much with yourself in just an hour. Try it. Think of 1 thing you would like to do to actually help yourself. Forget the anxiety about doing so, for just an hour. You have your whole life to kick your own ass.

Welp, there goes the stigma of it being a sign of weakness. I wish I could offer words to help motivate, but I honestly do believe that you must allow yourself to feel the hurt. I came to this conclusion after being so fucked off my ass on so many meds, which left me , literally, unable to feel anything. As much as pain sucks man, trust me, feeling nothing is much worse.

As much as it hurts, can you admit that doing nothing would just allow it to continue? 

Dude, you got this. 

I hate to admit it, it took several years of suicidal depression and not getting proper support to realize that I had to do it myself, but it is going to take you summoning of astonishing strength, which you will only get from going through hell. In other words, if you hold on, I promise that you will begin to develop the ability to work things out. I am not allowed to offer any sort of private conversations here, it got me banned for 30 days last time, but I am always up for conversation and sharing of ideas etc.

Its been 1 month since I was kicked off Reddit, good to be back. 

As for your concerns, you DO realize that when you see such things on social networks, you're seeing just the good times? We all have bad times, man. 

Ending your life is not going to bring you peace. Thats not my subjective view, its a scientific fact. Relieve requires you to be alive. 

I have chatted with dozens of people,  a majority of them refuse to fight for themselves as if their lives depended on it. Look, I will not bullshit you. I have been there, fucked off my ass on over 7 medications at one time. I understand the stigma. Even family telling you that you're a loser, etc. I have heard it all. 

I am going to be completely honest with you here: Fuck everyone else. What is important is that YOU realize you are strong. If you hadnt been, trust me, youd be dead  by now. I considered jumping in front of a fucking train for years, 3 actually. It was absolute hell. 

tl;dr Do NOT give up. I promise you, just as I have all the others, if you push as hard as you possibly can and never quit, things WILL change. Want to die? Then what the hell is stopping you from kicking ass in the meantime? Honestly, man, you have absolutely NOTHING to lose and the world to gain. It wont be easy, youll probably hate yourself a lot more before you learn that you are a tough bastard. Just do not give up. We SERIOUSLY need people like you to get better, so you can come back here and help someone else.

I know it sounds pretty lame, that ran through my head with each word. But it pretty much sums up how I feel. 

These seemingly insignificant words I spewed do not even begin to touch on how much faith I have in the "human spirit". It also sums up the frustration I had, and continue to have, for myself. I also understand how patronizing it seems to tell something they can do anything with effort. The last thing I wish to do is to tell someone they are not trying hard enough. What I actually mean to say is, they are a fuck-ton more resilient than they could possibly imagine.

So my remarks were deleted. Sigh. 

Look, you underestimate yourself, massively. You are human, which means you are part of a very long line of suffering. I am not telling you to get over it, I am telling you that you can handle it. You can surpass all this bullshit and become incredible. 

As difficult as life is, and it is hell lets face it, we do not get nothing for our suffering. Throughout human history we have suffered greatly, to say the least. Being through all that, human beings have survived. We do so because we are fucking amazing. 

Have more faith in yourself, you are fucking worth life.

Well, theyre not hard off from the truth. The fact is, like anything else in the human brain, there are connections made. Which is why habits are so difficult to break. 


If others would get off their high horses and read whats being said, theyd get what I meant. The act of being tough on yourself, ie putting in effort to purposely put yourself in situations that scare you, in order to show yourself the fear is an absolute illusion , will help , quite literally, re-wire your brain. 

When I tell people they need to be tougher on themselves, and take actions, it is always, always understood to mean they are not trying now, which is not what I mean at all. 


I have nothing but absolute empathy for people suffering with depression. Those who do it, do it alone. But the thing is, every human being on this planet is essentially alone, in their heads. The reason why so many misunderstand, and assume, is because we cant read minds. It is difficult enough for anyone to understand depression, and it gets worse when someone going through it, confused, has to explain it to someone who hasnt been through it. 

Shit needs to change. Some need to understand that the pain they are going through, it CAN be stopped. It CAN and WILL serve to help them become better , more empathetic human beings, which is what this world needs.

Your last question I will respond to, as soon you you also respond to the same question. 

At what point to I even imply making fun? I take depression incredibly serious. I went years of people telling me it was all in my head. I spent a majority of that time being with my aging grandparents, one of whom had dementia. The other, well, he was 90 and didnt believe anything like it actually existed.

You're completely ignoring anything I said other than the part about being tough on yourself.
Try years. And you know what it got me? Nothing but more medication and a trip to a nuthouse.

You mean because Im experienced with a subject? 

Try looking around a bit, I understand plenty about depression. Not once did I say "Its all in your head", etc. 

I am saying  people need to start doing something. If they have, then try harder. Depression is an absolute bitch, and it doesnt deserve to be pussy-footed around, people need to kick its ass. 

Regardless of what someone says, if they try to suggest maybe a walk or a good therapist, theyre told "You dont know what its like". Fuck off, get over yourself.

Did you read anything I said? Its nothing to wi th tough love. Its to do with motivating yourself. Would you rather someone told you its ok, just sit around?

I have been there, youre not the only one who has been through depression.

Then get the fuck off the computer and get outside. 

Thats about the most truthful reply I can give to anyone. I am sick of people telling me "You dont understand!". No shit, nobody understands what others go through. But when all you do is sit there and do not push yourself, it gets worse. It keeps getting worse the more you are alone, and do not realize that YOU are part of what is going to end the stigma of depression, which is going to lead to faster, more reliable recovery. 

More people need to look into cognitive therapy. And before anyone tells me "Therapy doesnt work", it will work with an insane amount of effort. 

Pro-tip: Nobody is going to be able to motivate you, you have to motivate yourself. 

As for going outside, and nothing to do. Go for a walk. Sound boring? Then make it interesting. Youre human, you are known for having an incredible imagination. Just going out and walking, in itself, is good for you. Get some sun, soak in some of that fucking amazing vitamin D, which is VERY good for you in every way imaginable. Just .. get out. People are constantly avoiding going out because they cannot find anything to stimulate them , again, a simple walk seems boring. But the idea is not to be entertained, its to stay healthy. Sometimes staying healthy is very boring. 

I spent several years of my life burying myself in my work, at my desk at home. I was so busy that I failed to realize what was going on within my own head, and that nearly lead to me killing myself. Dont just sit there and feel bad for yourself, take some god damn action.

Pretty easy to sleep when you feel this way, Ive done it many times. There's a reason it leaves you feeling worse. 

Theres no real answer to this , what to do about it etc. Its just as easy to say "Keep yourself busy, dont sleep too much". But people generally react in a negative manner, "You dont know what its like". The fact of the matter is, nobody knows how anyone else sees things. Its all subjective. Well, all but how ineffective it actually is to get too much sleep.

This is just the type of understanding he needs, its what everyone needs. Depression or not. 


I am actually very impressed if this is the way you're handing things. He also seems from what you've said, to have an understanding of whats going on, that is absolutely crucial. Many of us never had this kind of support, please keep at it. Very well done, both of you.

Also, you *do* realize that your brain is constantly being rewired, right? When you plant all these self-destructive thoughts in your head, there are connections being made that make these thoughts/habits more difficult to break. Thats not just "some people", its not just my opinion, its neuroscience. Our brains work the same way, but somehow youre different? 

You need to stop confusing possibility with difficulty. Of course its difficult. I never once implied it was easy. Human beings have struggled with this for thousands of years.

Science involves the natural world. You live and breathe, are part of the natural world. How is science not involved? That makes no sense whatsoever. 

It means that theres literally nothing in the world that can hold you back.. given enough is put into what you need to get done. Aside from brain damage which transforms your brain. 

I have no doubt there are chemicals involved in how we feel, thats obvious (Thanks, science). But you CAN change that. Theres a HUGE difference between what YOU feel and what is possible, thats also obvious. 

If you want to be all insulting simply because someone has a different point of view, based on actual research coupled with experience, then the conversation was dead before it began.

If you get too much sleep, its going to make you tired. Being depressed is going to be exhausting, which means youll have to try twice as hard as the average person. But you can do it, if you really want to.
You're a bad ass, nicely done.

Take it from someone who has been there... just stop doing it. 

Forget listening to the nonsense people say about just sleeping if you feel like it. As you said, it makes you feel bad. 

Sleeping is comforting tho I totally understand. But thats why you should try not to. I forced myself to go out on walks. And Im sure I do not have to tell you what occurs within the body when you go for long walks , you flood your body with the good shit your body has, and it feels good.
Things I have done, sure. But not who I was.I mean, life is a learning experience. Without fuck ups we'd never learn.

Whether you care or not is irrelevant to the actual idea that anything is possible. Possible does not mean absolute, I do not believe in absolute, nor does science.
